libraries.name: Bluetooth (HC-05)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The HC-05 Bluetooth serial module: whatever a phone sends comes out of its TXD as serial bytes, and whatever the board sends to its RXD goes to the phone. The phone is in the run panel: type a line and Send. Use SoftwareSerial or Serial1/Serial2.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Buzzers
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: An active buzzer (beeps by itself when powered) and a passive buzzer (plays the note you give it with tone()). You hear them: the toolbar's Sound button turns part sounds on and off.

libraries.name: Climate sensors
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Temperature and humidity: the DHT11 and DHT22 (one data wire) and the BME280 (I2C, with air pressure). Set the weather with sliders in the run panel. Includes DHT.h and Adafruit_BME280.h.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Colour-tracking camera
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A small camera that finds the biggest patch of one colour (red, green, blue, yellow...) in what it sees and tells a board where it is over I2C, like the Pixy or HuskyLens cameras robots use. A screen on its back shows what it sees. Includes BlobCam.h for sketches.

libraries.name: Gear motor with encoder
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The yellow TT gear motor with a 20-slot encoder disc and an optical sensor on its shaft: its OUT pin changes as the slots pass, so a board can count how far and how fast it turned. Drive it like any TT motor (through a motor driver).

libraries.name: IR remote and receiver
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The little 21-key infrared remote and an IR receiver module (VS1838B). Press the remote's keys in the run panel; every receiver on the bench picks up the code (NEC protocol). Includes IRremote.h, both its new (IrReceiver) and old (IRrecv) ways.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Line, obstacle, laser and motion sensors
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Sensors robots use: the TCRT5000 line sensor (sees dark lines on a light floor), the FC-51 obstacle sensor (IR, a few cm), the VL53L0X laser distance sensor (I2C, up to 2 m) and the HC-SR501 PIR motion sensor. They really look at the bench. Includes VL53L0X.h and Adafruit_VL53L0X.h.

libraries.name: Joystick and rotary encoder
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A thumb joystick (KY-023: two knobs and a push button) and a rotary encoder knob (KY-040: clicks round in steps, and pushes). Work them from the run panel.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Keypads
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Membrane keypads (4x4 and 4x3): each key joins its row wire to its column wire while it's held, exactly as the real ones do. Press the keys in the run panel. Includes Keypad.h.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: LCD 16x2 (I2C)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The classic blue 16x2 character LCD (HD44780) with an I2C backpack (PCF8574): text on 2 lines over just 2 wires. Includes LiquidCrystal_I2C.h for sketches; real firmware using LiquidCrystal_I2C works too.

libraries.name: LCD 16x2 green (parallel, LiquidCrystal)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A 16x2 character LCD (HD44780) with green text, wired the classic parallel way: RS, E and four data pins, as in Arduino's LiquidCrystal examples. Includes LiquidCrystal.h for sketches. Needs its contrast pin (V0) set, like the real one.

libraries.name: LED matrix 8x8 (MAX7219)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The common red 8x8 LED matrix module with a MAX7219 driver: 64 LEDs from 3 pins (DIN, CS, CLK). Includes LedControl.h for sketches.

libraries.name: NeoPixel LEDs (WS2812B)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Addressable RGB LEDs (WS2812B, "NeoPixels"): a stick of 8, a strip of 30 and an 8x8 panel. One data wire sets every LED's colour; chain them DOUT to DIN. Includes Adafruit_NeoPixel.h.

libraries.name: OLED display (SSD1306)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The little I2C OLED screens (SSD1306): 128x64 and 128x32 pixels, white, blue or yellow-and-blue. Text, lines, shapes and pictures with Adafruit_SSD1306.h and Adafruit_GFX.h. The part speaks the real SSD1306 commands.

libraries.name: Relay module
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A 5 V relay on a module: a board's pin switches a separate circuit (a lamp, a motor, a pump) through its COM, NO and NC contacts. It clicks.

libraries.name: Stepper motors
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Two stepper motors with their drivers: the small 28BYJ-48 on a ULN2003 board (4 pins) and a NEMA 17 on an A4988 driver (STEP and DIR). They turn exactly as many steps as they're given, hold their position, and skip steps when overloaded or rushed. Includes Stepper.h and AccelStepper.h.

libraries.name: 4-digit display (TM1637)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The red 4-digit 7-segment display with a colon (a clock display) on a TM1637 chip: two wires, CLK and DIO. Includes TM1637Display.h. The part decodes the real TM1637 signals bit by bit.
